findings.title: Pod's DNS settings leave out cluster DNS
findings.cause: container api exits because payments does not resolve: the pod sets dnsPolicy None, so its resolv.conf has only its dnsConfig (nameservers 1.1.1.1, search domains corp.example), and those do not answer for the cluster's Services; its log says: "wget: bad address 'payments:8080'"; Deployment api has 0 of 1 replicas ready

evidence.what: container api exited with code 1 (Error), restarted 5 times
last lines of container api's log (current run)
the pod sets dnsPolicy None, with nameservers 1.1.1.1 and search domains corp.example
evidence.command: kubectl get pod api-5c4f64b4b7-65m6c -n kd-dnspolicy-none -o jsonpath='{.spec.dnsPolicy}{" "}{.spec.dnsConfig}'

findings.fix: Use dnsPolicy ClusterFirst and put extra nameservers or search domains in dnsConfig, which ClusterFirst adds to cluster DNS; or, keeping None, list the cluster DNS Service's IP (kubectl get svc -n kube-system kube-dns) and the search domains kd-dnspolicy-none.svc.cluster.local, svc.cluster.local and cluster.local.
